# Section A — Multiple Choice

### Question 1

Which statement best matches the lecture discussion of **How to kill a dopamine neuron**?

- **A.** Nigrostriatal tract facilitates voluntary movement. Research on the motor functions of DA:.
- **B.** Apomorphine: agonist that stimulates D1 and D2 receptors; causes behavioral activation. Amphetamine: drug that enhances dopamine release Relatively more dopamine on intact side.
- **C.** Dopamine-deficient (DD) mouse: gene for TH is knocked out but not the gene for DBH – NE can be synthesized but not DA. DD mice exhibit severe aphagia (lack of feeding behavior), adipsia (lack of drinking), and hypoactivity; behaviors can be restored by L-DOPA.
- **D.** Mesolimbic dopamine pathway activates arousal and locomotor behavior; different neurons mediate the effects of rewarding and aversive stimuli. Mesocortical pathway: input to the PFC helps regulate cognitive functions such as attention and working memory.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Answer"}
**Correct answer: A.**
Nigrostriatal tract facilitates voluntary movement. Research on the motor functions of DA:.
:::

**Source:** Lecture 5, topic **How to kill a dopamine neuron**. The correct option matches the relationship taught for that topic; the alternatives are course concepts drawn from other parts of the same lecture and do not fit this stem.

### Question 3

Which statement best matches the lecture discussion of **Electrophysiological properties of serotonin neurons**?

- **A.** First demonstrated in cats: when awake, each nerve cell fires at a regular rate (tonic firing); become irregular with slow-wave sleep and stop firing during REM sleep. Research with DRN and MRN knockout mice: slow, tonic firing of DRN neurons promotes sleep (non-REM sleep); burst firing of the same cells favors a state of wakefulness.
- **B.** 14 receptor subtypes; 5-HT1A and 5-HT2A are most well known. 5-HT1A receptors: concentrated in the hippocampus, septal area, amygdala, and DRN; inhibit adenylyl cyclase to decrease cAMP synthesis; increase opening of K+ channels and membrane hyperpolarization 5-HT1A.
- **C.** 5-HT2A receptors occur in the cortex and other brain areas. Function via the phosphoinositide second- messenger system: increases Ca2+ levels in the postsynaptic cell; also activates protein kinase C (PKC).
- **D.** Ligand binds to a GPCR/receptor. The receptor activates PLC (phospholipase C).

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Answer"}
**Correct answer: A.**
First demonstrated in cats: when awake, each nerve cell fires at a regular rate (tonic firing); become irregular with slow-wave sleep and stop firing during REM sleep. Research with DRN and MRN knockout mice: slow, tonic firing of DRN neurons promotes sleep (non-REM sleep); burst firing of the same cells favors a state of wakefulness.
:::

::: {.callout-note .question-explanation collapse="true" title="Explanation"}
**Source:** Lecture 7, topic **Electrophysiological properties of serotonin neurons**. The correct option matches the relationship taught for that topic; the alternatives are course concepts drawn from other parts of the same lecture and do not fit this stem.
:::
